clue.text: Spin without beginning to unravel

indicators.note: the word for spin loses its opening letter, the one at its beginning

parts.note: to spin is to revolve

explanation.surface: A spinning thread starts to come undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without beginning' drops the R from REVOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The original Latin sense of the verb is to unroll or unfold, so it can mean unravel.

clue.text: Millions getting lost in woman's song

indicators.note: the millions are removed from the woman's name, so that letter goes missing

parts.note: Maria is a woman's name
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A singer loses millions on a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting lost' takes M out of MARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo piece for one voice is a kind of song.

clue.text: Two kinds of fuel sent up to cover the Queen's women's quarters

indicators.note: the fuels go around the royal abbreviation, covering it
in a down clue the fuels are read from bottom to top

parts.note: oil is one fuel
gas is another fuel
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Fuel is shipped to supply the Queen's household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns OILGAS into SAGLIO; 'to cover' puts ER inside, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem, the secluded part of a Muslim palace where wives and concubines lived, is this.

clue.text: Speed of progress through life

definitions.meaning: to rush along headlong at full tilt
one's working course or profession over the years

explanation.surface: How fast one gets on in life.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means hurtle along; as a noun it means a person's course through working life.

clue.text: Note this accommodation could be for two families

definitions.meaning: a musical note lowered by two semitones

definitions.text: this accommodation could be for two families
definitions.meaning: read literally, an apartment for a pair of households

explanation.surface: A remark that a property might house two households.
explanation.definitionFit: In music it is a sign lowering a pitch two semitones; read literally it is a flat for two.

clue.text: Religious orders

parts.note: orders here are commands or rules laid down by the Church, not monastic communities

explanation.surface: Monks, nuns and friars in their communities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' suggests monastic brotherhoods, but here it means decrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Church law is the body of rules issued by ecclesiastical authority, which are religious commands.

clue.text: PTO to see it

parts.note: PTO is 'please turn over', telling the reader the continuation is on the reverse side

explanation.surface: An instruction at the foot of a page to turn it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means on the other side of the page, which is where turning over takes you.

clue.text: Elector all at sea?

parts.note: a voter unsure which party to back, pictured as adrift on the waves

explanation.surface: A voter who is confused or lost.
explanation.definitionFit: An undecided voter not committed to any party drifts between them, like something bobbing at sea.

clue.text: In the morning exam, not bothered if it's right or wrong

definitions.text: not bothered if it's right or wrong

parts.note: AM abbreviates ante meridiem, before noon
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A student sitting an early test doesn't care about getting answers right.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking any moral sense is indifferent to whether conduct is good or bad.

clue.text: A hat the French female brought back in fleecy wool

indicators.note: the whole string of pieces is returned, read from its end to its start

parts.note: a cap is a hat
la is the feminine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman returns with a hat made of soft wool.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fleece of a South American relative of the llama gives a fine wool of this name.

clue.text: Love writer — reserve one that's easy to read

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a pen is a writing instrument
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: A romance novelist books something easy to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person whose thoughts and feelings are plain to see is readily understood.

clue.text: In every rota going round, insert colonel as coffee-maker

indicators.note: the colonel is put into the middle of the combined string

parts.note: per means for each, every

indicators.note: the rota is turned about and its letters rearranged

parts.note: Col is the military abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: An officer is added to the duty roster to make the coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link word; the colonel goes inside the whole string after 'every' and the reworked rota, not into the rota alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot that circulates boiling water through ground beans is a device for brewing the drink.

clue.text: 'Bout of weeping got pram fixed' — could be a coded message?

parts.note: a cry is a spell of tears

indicators.note: the words are repaired, i.e. put into a new order

explanation.surface: A crying baby whose pram was repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A text written in cipher is a message whose meaning is concealed by a code.

clue.text: Liberal, fifty, being hugged by each woman

indicators.note: the two letters sit inside the abbreviation, embraced by it

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old Liberal embraced by every woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it stands for a female person.

clue.text: Enforce order with redistribution of wealth — took a nap first

indicators.note: the nap phrase comes before the rest of the answer

parts.note: to have lain down is to have rested

indicators.note: the letters of wealth are shared out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A politician sleeps before imposing a wealth-sharing policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for issuing authoritative commands and insisting they be obeyed.

clue.text: Cromarty's partner wearing flimsy fabric, being game

indicators.note: the partner has the fabric on, so the fabric goes round it

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric
Ross and Cromarty is a former Scottish county, so Ross partners Cromarty

explanation.surface: A Scot dressed in delicate fabric is playing a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross and Cromarty was a county in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A field sport played with netted sticks is a game.

clue.text: Attractive employee takes part

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in a farmhand
some means a portion of something

explanation.surface: A good-looking worker takes a role.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a good-looking person is pleasing to the eye.

clue.text: National racecourse — leader's abandoned

indicators.note: the racecourse name drops its leading letter

parts.note: Ascot is an English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: At the Grand National the leading horse has been withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English racecourse; 'leader's abandoned' drops its A. 'National' suggests the Grand National horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: A national here means a citizen of a country, here one from Scotland.

clue.text: Warn of collapse, no longer frozen?

parts.note: to give is to yield or collapse under pressure
read as two words, without frost: not ice

explanation.surface: Cautioning that a thawed structure might fall in.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally inform someone in advance, e.g. that a job or tenancy will end, is to warn them.

clue.text: Some characters here began netting bird

indicators.note: only some of the letters in the following words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Someone here has started catching a bird in a net.
explanation.definitionFit: A large white seabird that dives for fish is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Money you and I raised for something to eat — that's nutty

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: in a down clue the pronoun is lifted, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: we means you and I

explanation.surface: We raise money for a snack that's a bit mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's nutty' confirms the type of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidney-shaped nut is an edible snack.

clue.text: Head's put by cash for cake

indicators.note: the head word is placed next to, after, the money word

parts.note: dough is slang for money
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A headteacher saves money to buy a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring or ball of fried sweet dough is a small cake.

clue.text: Showy display page penned by hack

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the page letter sits inside the hack word

parts.note: to hack is to slash

explanation.surface: A tabloid hack writes a sensational page.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a splash is to put on an ostentatious, eye-catching show.

clue.text: Man's post redirected

indicators.note: the post is sent back the other way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: post means mail

explanation.surface: A man's letters are forwarded to a new address.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, so it stands for a male person.

clue.text: Welcome break from porridge?

parts.note: porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, so a break from it is a breakout

explanation.surface: A pleasant change from eating oatmeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' is British slang for time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A jailbreak is getting free of a prison sentence, a break that is welcome to the convict.

clue.text: Gatecrasher called and stormed

parts.note: a battering ram crashes through gates
paged means summoned over a system

explanation.surface: An uninvited guest was summoned and stormed off.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge about violently and destructively is to storm around.
